newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips close higher on funds support.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips close higher on funds support.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip shares closed sharply higher on Wednesday as foreign and local institutions bought up cheapened index-linked stocks, analysts and dealers said.
The benchmark Composite Index closed 16.06 points, 1.58 percent, higher at 1,034.07. The small-capitalised Second Board index closed 5.98 points, 1.11 percent, higher at 542.33.
"There's some foreign buying out of Hong Kong on our side," said a dealer at a Malaysian brokerage. "It's about time as most of the stocks are quite cheap," she added.
Key index stocks Telekom, Petronas Gas and Tenaga led the surge, as they account for around 25 percent of the weighting of the Composite Index. The stocks rose between 20 and 50 cents.
"It looks like they (institutional funds) have been buying Petronas Gas, Tenaga and Telekom," said Ken Loo, head of research at Amsteel Securities.
"The PM (Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad) is back, and I am confident the ringgit will strengthen, and that the Bakun issues will be solved now," said a dealer at a local bank-backed brokerage.
Mahathir had left for a two-month sabatical in May. Since then the ringgit has come under speculative attack, pushing it to a 38-month low earlier in July.

Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has said last week of disagreements between Ekran, main developer, and Asea Brown Boveri, the chief contractor, of the $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam in Sarawak state.

Timber and plywood maker Sinora gained 1.25 ringgit to 8.00 ringgit on what dealers and analysts described as a "pure syndicate play". The stock was the most actively-traded, with 12.4 million shares changing hands.

Household sanitary products maker Unza was the day's highest gainer, rising 6.40 ringgit to 22.20 ringgit, after hitting a new year high at 23.30 ringgit. Its shares were requoted on Wednesday morning after its parent company Berjaya Singer had earlier announced plans to divest its interests in Unza.

Wall Street's record overnight close on Tuesday did not significantly impact sentiment locally, although the prospects of an easing interest rate environment in the U.S. would augur well for the Malaysian economy, said analysts.
The Dow Jones industrial average jumped 154.93 points to 8,061.65 after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's congressional testimony contained no unsettling remarks.
Market volume in Kuala Lumpur stood at 232 million shares, valued at 1.55 billion ringgit. Gainers outpaced losers 526 to 111.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot July contract gained 24.0 points to 1,016.0 with 1,224 lots traded. August futures closed 24.6 points higher, also to 1,016.0, with 204 lots changing hands.
